content:
{
  "root_cause": "The modal's focus trap only returns focus when focus leaves the modal; it does not prevent shift+tab from moving focus from the first focusable element (close button) to the opener button outside the modal. Consequently, focus leaves the modal, the focusin listener returns focus to the modal element itself, and the expected wrap to the last focusable element (delete button) does not occur.",
  "repair_strategy": "Add tab trapping logic to the modal's existing keydown listener (bound to EVENT_KEYDOWN_DISMISS) to intercept Tab and Shift+Tab when the active element is the first or last focusable item inside the modal, prevent default, and move focus to the opposite end. Also add a helper method _getFocusableElements that returns a list of focusable controls within the modal using standard selectors and the isDisabled utility.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Shift+Tab from the first control (close button) will now wrap to the Delete button, allowing continuous reverse navigation within the modal without focus escaping to the opener button.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Custom keyboard handling in modal content could interfere with the added tab logic.",
    "If the modal contains non-standard focusable elements not covered by the selector list, wrapping may behave unexpectedly.",
    "Changes to the modal's DOM structure after show (e.g., dynamic insertion) could cause the focusable list to be stale until the next shown event."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that Tab moves focus: close button → input field → cancel button → delete button → then wraps back to close button.",
    "Verify that Shift+Tab moves focus: delete button → cancel button → input field → close button → then wraps back to delete button.",
    "Confirm that Escape key still closes the modal as before.",
    "Ensure that after modal closure, focus returns to the element that triggered the modal (the Delete project button).",
    "Check that dynamically added or removed controls inside the modal are respected when the modal is re‑shown."
  ]
}
